title: Old, stopped: quadratic reciprocity with fair prompts, but searches counted against the labs' money, so shared and OSO turns still cost more (Nov 27)
question: With the same prompt size in every setup (60 lemmas shown: the newest and those related to the lab's recent tries; the rest found by search), and a lemma already in the library telling the lab its name and letting it try again, does OSO get further into quadratic reciprocity than working alone or a shared library, for the same $4 a run? Replaces qr-2. One run each: a first look. [A]
answer: Stopped early (about round 85, $0.70–0.81 of $4 a run), not a result. Prompts were the same size in every setup, but each library search cost the lab a reply from its own money, and shared and OSO labs searched about three times as often as traditional ones, so their turns cost about a quarter more. The next run makes searches free to the labs.

targets.text: Quadratic reciprocity, from scratch: for two different odd primes p and q, q is a square remainder mod p exactly when p is one mod q, unless both p and q leave remainder 3 when divided by 4; then exactly one of them is.
